title: Lower Shell Below the Belly Fairing — Pre-Qualified Doubler Family for Impact Damage

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Permanent external doubler repair for ground impact damage on the lower shell below the belly fairing, in four pre-qualified sizes with a common fastener pattern and a selection chart keyed to the measured damage.

sections.purpose: This repair covers dents, scratches and small punctures on the lower shell panels below the belly fairing, using one of four pre-qualified doubler sizes selected from the damage measurements.
sections.damage_assessment: Measure the damage length, width and depth, and the distance to the nearest fastener row and to the nearest frame or stringer. The family admits damage up to 120 millimetres in the longest dimension, up to 2.5 millimetres deep after cleaning, no closer than 20 millimetres to a fastener row and no closer than 40 millimetres to a frame or stringer. Only one repair per bay is admitted, and a bay that already carries a repair from this family is outside the scope. Damage with any crack, however short, is outside the family regardless of size and needs a repair approval request.
sections.repair_procedure: Clean the area and remove the damaged material to a smooth blend, keeping the blend radius above 25 millimetres and the removal depth inside the limit. Select the doubler size from the chart against the blended dimensions. Position the doubler concentric with the blend and mark the fastener pattern with the drill jig, holding the edge distance at 15 millimetres minimum. Drill the pattern, deburr and clean. Apply the primer to both faying surfaces and let it dry to touch. Apply the faying surface sealant, position the doubler and install the fasteners wet, working from the centre outward. Remove the extruded sealant and form the fillet. On the two larger sizes, install the cleat at the forward edge and the gusset at the aft edge as shown on the repair drawing. Restore the external protection scheme and apply the repair stencil with the family reference and the date.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection of the fastener rows immediately after installation to establish the baseline, and record it in the structural repair record. Repeat the eddy current inspection at 6 000 flight cycles and then at each subsequent 4 000 flight cycles. Do a detailed visual inspection of the doubler edges and the sealant fillet at every A check. Any indication at a fastener hole, or any lifted edge, ends the repair life and requires a repair approval request.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Damage up to 120 mm in the longest dimension and 2.5 mm deep after cleaning, not closer than 20 mm to a fastener row or 40 mm to a frame or stringer, one repair per bay, no cracking.

repair_drawings.title: Pre-qualified doubler family, lower shell below belly fairing, four sizes

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows at 22 mm pitch on the two smaller sizes, three rows at 20 mm pitch on the two larger sizes, 15 mm minimum edge distance
type_data.fatigue_life_note: The repair is life limited to 24 000 flight cycles from installation. A repeat eddy current inspection is required at 6 000 cycles and then every 4 000 cycles.
